children: Australia's 2Q GDP contained a twist that will bring the Reserve Bank of Australia closer to raising interest rates again, says Paul Bloxham, chief economist at HSBC, Australia. The data confirms that the economy still has a very weak supply-side, with labor productivity falling. GDP per hour worked dropped 0.2% from a year ago, he says. It means that despite more hours being worked, there's less output occurring, not more. The speed limit for the economy is very low at present and the pace of GDP growth is currently beating it, he adds. (james.glynn@wsj.com; X @JamesGlynnWSJ)
